start.title: The First Light
start.text:
Spices in hand, you walk before sunrise.
Who will roll the great stone away?

choices.text: Turn back. It is too heavy
choices.feedback: Hope must keep walking.
Mark 16:3 — The women wondered among themselves who would roll away the stone for them.
Love does not wait at dawn.

turn_consequence.title: Do Not Turn
turn_consequence.text:
Grief calls you to honor His body.
The path is shorter than the fear.

choices.feedback: Your feet find the path again.

wait_consequence.title: Go Now
wait_consequence.text:
Some hopes cannot wait for morning.
The spices are in your hands.

choices.feedback: You press on toward the tomb.

stone.title: The Stone Is Moved
stone.text:
The great stone lies rolled aside.
The tomb gapes open in the dawn.

choices.feedback: Fear cannot guard a miracle.
No human hand did this.
Luke 24:3 — The women entered the tomb after finding the stone rolled away.

run_consequence.title: Do Not Flee Yet
run_consequence.text:
Truth waits inside the open door.
Go near. See what God has done.

choices.feedback: You move toward the threshold.

accuse_consequence.title: Not Theft
accuse_consequence.text:
No grave robber leaves linen folded.
This is something far greater.

choices.feedback: You step softly into the light.

enter.title: Linen Cloths Lying
enter.text:
The slab is bare. Folded cloths remain.
His body is not here.

choices.feedback: Lift your eyes. Heaven is speaking.
John 20:5-7 — Peter and John saw the linen cloths lying there, and the napkin that had been around Jesus' head, not lying with the linen cloths but folded up in a place by itself.

choices.text: Touch the folded cloths in anger
choices.feedback: Anger blinds the eye to glory.

weep_consequence.title: Lift Your Eyes
weep_consequence.text:
Tears are right, but look up now.
You are not alone in this place.

choices.feedback: Light pours across the stone.

anger_consequence.title: Not Anger
anger_consequence.text:
Linen folded with care is no theft.
Look up. See who waits with you.

choices.feedback: Your hands fall open in awe.

angels.title: Two Shining Ones
angels.text:
Two figures in white ask softly,
"Why seek the living among the dead?"

choices.feedback: Listen first. Hope is speaking.
He is not lost. He is risen.
Luke 24:4-5 — Two men in dazzling apparel stood by the women and asked why they were seeking the living among the dead.

argue_consequence.title: Be Still and Hear
argue_consequence.text:
Your grief is heard, but listen now.
This is a message you must carry.

choices.feedback: You bow your head in reverence.

demand_consequence.title: He Is Not Held
demand_consequence.text:
No tomb can keep what God has raised.
Be still and hear the truth.

choices.feedback: Stillness opens your heart.

message.title: He Is Risen
message.text:
"He is not here. He is risen,
as He told you in Galilee."

choices.feedback: Remember what He promised.
Luke 24:6-7 — The angels reminded the women that Jesus had told them He must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again.

choices.text: Boast that you knew all along
choices.feedback: Humility carries this news.

doubt_consequence.title: Trust His Word
doubt_consequence.text:
He said on the third day He would rise.
Let His promise meet your heart.

choices.feedback: Memory becomes light within you.

boast_consequence.title: Not Pride
boast_consequence.text:
This news is not yours to wear.
It is yours to carry, gently.

choices.feedback: You lower your head in awe.

remember.title: Run with the News
remember.text:
The other women wait, pale with fear.
What will you do with this hope?

choices.feedback: Hope must be spoken aloud.

choices.text: Tell them. Go to the disciples
choices.feedback: Luke 24:9 — The women returned from the tomb and reported all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.
Good news has no riddles.

silent_consequence.title: Speak It Out
silent_consequence.text:
A locked heart cannot carry light.
Let the joy run from your lips.

choices.text: Tell them. Go to the disciples
choices.feedback: Your voice trembles with joy.

test_consequence.title: Plain Words
test_consequence.text:
Tell them clearly. The tomb is empty.
He is risen, as He said.

choices.text: Tell them. Go to the disciples
choices.feedback: Plain truth opens every ear.

disciples.title: Peter and John
disciples.text:
Peter stares. John leans in.
"The Lord is risen," you say.

choices.feedback: Blame poisons holy news.
Luke 24:10 — Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James and the other women with them told these things to the apostles.

choices.text: Beg them to come prove it
choices.feedback: They already believe enough to run.

blame_consequence.title: Not Blame, Joy
blame_consequence.text:
Their hiding will turn to running soon.
Give them only the good news.

choices.feedback: John's eyes fill with light.

beg_consequence.title: Steady, Not Begging
beg_consequence.text:
Truth needs no pleading to be true.
Stand and tell them plainly.

choices.feedback: They rise and follow you.

sunrise.title: The Promise Fulfilled
sunrise.text:
The sun crests the hills. Death is undone.
What fills your heart now?

choices.feedback: Hope, not fear, has the last word.
Matthew 28:8 — The women departed quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, and ran to tell His disciples.
Joy belongs to everyone now.

fear_end_consequence.title: Hope Wins
fear_end_consequence.text:
Death itself has been undone today.
No fear can outlast that light.

choices.feedback: Peace settles over your heart.

pride_end_consequence.title: Joy for All
pride_end_consequence.text:
This morning is not a prize won.
It is a gift to share with everyone.

choices.feedback: You open your hands to the sky.

ending.title: He Is Risen Indeed
ending.text:
The grave is empty. The promise stands.
Death has lost. Hope has won.
